input: Learn basic car maintenance like oil changes

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: "Basic maintenance" could mean just oil changes, or it could extend to tire rotation, air filters, brake pads, fluid top-ups, etc. The scope determines how large and long the learning plan needs to be.
Knowing whether this is for themselves alone, or also to help a family member or teach someone else, changes the depth and framing of the plan.
Whether the user has access to a garage, driveway, or only a parking lot affects which tasks are physically feasible and what equipment is needed.
A tight budget affects whether they can buy tools and supplies, or whether they should focus on knowledge first and pay a shop for now.
Their preferred learning format — videos, hands-on practice, a course, a manual — determines how to structure the actual learning steps.
Success could mean being able to do an oil change solo, passing a knowledge quiz, or confidently handling roadside issues. This defines what 'done' looks like.
Some people want to go deep on the 'why' (mechanical understanding), others just want a repeatable checklist. This shapes the tone and depth of all content.

gold.taskTitle: Learn basic car maintenance starting with oil changes
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn how to perform basic car maintenance, using oil changes as a starting point, but the scope, context, and learning approach still need to be defined.

questions.title: Which maintenance tasks do you want to cover beyond oil changes?
questions.description: Does the user want to stop at oil changes, or include things like tire rotation, air filters, brake inspection, and fluid checks?

questions.title: Are you learning this for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the plan is personal skill-building or also meant to help or teach another person.

questions.title: Where will you be doing the work — garage, driveway, or elsewhere?
questions.description: The available workspace determines which tasks are feasible and what safety or equipment considerations apply.

questions.title: How much are you willing to spend on tools and supplies?
questions.description: Budget determines whether to prioritize buying tools now or focus on learning before investing in equipment.

questions.title: Do you prefer learning through videos, hands-on practice, or written guides?
questions.description: The preferred learning format shapes which resources and steps are recommended first.

questions.title: What does success look like — doing a task solo, or just understanding it?
questions.description: Defines the finish line: is the goal to physically complete a maintenance task independently, or to build foundational knowledge?

questions.title: Do you want to understand how things work, or follow a checklist?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan should go deep on mechanical concepts or stay practical and procedure-focused.
